classification.difficultyReason: Calculate and compare circle areas with square or triangle areas, halving diameters where required.

children.label: a
children.prompt: a circle of diameter $10\text{ cm}$ or a square of side length $8\text{ cm}$?

answer.worked:
The circle has radius $10\div2=5\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{circle}}&=\pi\times5^2\\A_{\text{circle}}&=25\pi\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{square}}&=8\times8\\A_{\text{square}}&=64\text{ cm}^2.\end{align*}$$
Since $25\pi>64$, the circle has the larger area.

children.label: b
children.prompt: a circle of radius $4\text{ cm}$ or a square of side length $7\text{ cm}$?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{circle}}&=\pi\times4^2\\A_{\text{circle}}&=16\pi\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{square}}&=7\times7\\A_{\text{square}}&=49\text{ cm}^2.\end{align*}$$
Since $16\pi>49$, the circle has the larger area.

children.label: c
children.prompt: a circle of diameter $12\text{ m}$ or a triangle with base $13\text{ m}$ and height $17\text{ m}$?

answer.worked:
The circle has radius $12\div2=6\text{ m}$.
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{circle}}&=\pi\times6^2\\A_{\text{circle}}&=36\pi\text{ m}^2\\A_{\text{triangle}}&=\frac12\times13\times17\\A_{\text{triangle}}&=110.5\text{ m}^2.\end{align*}$$
Since $36\pi>110.5$, the circle has the larger area.
